settings.question: What makes a tire "high-performance" or UHP?
settings.answer: UHP stands for ultra-high-performance — tires designed for sports cars, performance sedans, and tuned vehicles where dry-handling grip, wet braking, and high-speed stability are priorities over tread life and cold-weather usability. Speed ratings of W, Y, and (Y) — capable of sustained speeds over 270 km/h. Softer compounds, shorter sidewalls, asymmetric or directional tread patterns.

settings.question: Can I run UHP tires year-round in Calgary?
settings.answer: Only the UHP all-season variants (Michelin Pilot Sport A/S 4, Continental ExtremeContact DWS06 Plus, BFGoodrich g-Force COMP-2 A/S+). True UHP summer tires (Pilot Sport 5, Potenza Sport, Proxes Sport) harden below 7°C and become unsafe — pull them by late October and run dedicated winters Nov–Mar.

settings.question: How long do performance tires last?
settings.answer: UHP summer tires typically last 30,000–50,000 km on a sport sedan driven enthusiastically. UHP all-seasons (Pilot Sport A/S 4) run 70,000–90,000 km warranties. Track-day use or aggressive street driving shortens life — soft compound is what gives them grip, and that compound wears off faster.

settings.question: Are wider tires always better for performance?
settings.answer: Up to a point. Wider tires increase contact patch and dry grip, but they also add weight, raise rolling resistance, hurt fuel economy, and respond worse to standing water (aquaplaning risk). For most street-driven performance cars, the OE fitment width is the right answer — only go wider if you've also addressed wheel offset, fender clearance, and suspension geometry.

settings.heading: What separates UHP from regular tires
settings.intro:
Ultra-high-performance tires are built for vehicles where the priority order is: dry handling first, wet braking second, comfort and tread life last. They're a different product from touring or all-terrain tires — softer rubber compound, stiffer construction, asymmetric tread patterns, higher speed ratings.

Here's what changes when you go from a touring tire to a UHP tire:
settings.outro: If you don't need the dry-handling improvement — say you're running a daily-driver sedan with no enthusiast tuning — a quality touring tire delivers better tread life, comfort, and fuel economy. UHP is for when the grip improvement actually shows up in how you drive.

settings.heading: When performance tires are the right call
settings.right_title: Touring or all-terrain instead if you:
settings.summary: UHP rubber pays back when you actually drive your vehicle the way it was engineered to be driven. If you're commuting in a daily-driver sedan or crossover, a quality touring tire is the smarter pick — better tread life, ride comfort, and fuel economy. For Calgary winters, always pair a UHP summer tire with a set of dedicated winter tires, or run a UHP all-season year-round.
